seo_title: Free Consulting for Bloomington Nonprofits | Net Impact IU
seo_description: Net Impact IU student teams give Bloomington-area nonprofits free, semester-long consulting in marketing, fundraising, research, operations and data.
headline: Free consulting for Bloomington nonprofits
intro: Net Impact IU offers free, semester-long consulting to Bloomington-area nonprofits. A team of six IU students works on a project you define, meets with you regularly, and delivers finished work by the end of the semester.

services.name: Marketing and engagement
services.text: Social media, events and campaigns that reach your audience.

services.name: Fundraising and grant strategy
services.text: Grant research and fundraising plans to grow your funding.

services.name: Research and strategic insights
services.text: Data-driven research to inform your next decision.

services.name: Partnership development and outreach
services.text: Finding and building relationships with partners.

services.name: Operational efficiency
services.text: Assessing how your operations run and where they can improve.

services.name: Data analysis and optimization
services.text: Turning your data into better decisions and operations.

steps.title: Reach out
steps.text: Email us with a short description of your organization and the help you need.

steps.title: Get matched
steps.text: Projects are matched to student teams at the start of each semester.

steps.title: Work together
steps.text: Your team meets with you weekly or biweekly to scope and assign tasks.

steps.title: Get results
steps.text: The team delivers finished work by semester's end, and you share mid-semester and final feedback.

cta_text: To be considered for next semester, email us before the semester starts.
time_text: About 10 hours of your time over the semester gets 150+ hours of ours: 15x your time, at zero cost.

client_quote.quote: The team did far more than we expected. They turned our scattered ideas into a clear outreach and fundraising strategy, backed it with real community research, and left us with materials we still use every week. It felt like working with a professional firm.
